reproduction_target: Small-RNA-seq and total-RNA-seq analysis of Drosophila melanogaster testes across Segregation Distorter genotypes: read trimming (trim_galore / cutadapt), QC (FastQC), mapping to a heterochromatin-enriched genome assembly (Bowtie, Bowtie2, STAR), gene counting (HTSeq) and repeat counting via a custom proportional-counting script, differential expression (DESeq2), gene-set enrichment (PANGEA), WGCNA co-expression module analysis, and figure generation from R Markdown. Wet-lab work (fly stocks and crosses, CRISPR transgenics, RNA extraction, RT-PCR/qRT-PCR, RNA FISH, confocal imaging, k-value drive assays, library prep and Illumina sequencing) is out of computational-reproduction scope.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from the 'Total RNA Seq Analysis' and 'Small RNA Seq Analysis' Methods subsections, plus the figure-generation step evidenced by the repository README prose (Rsp_SD_Figures.rmd). The repository (https://github.com/LarracuenteLab/SD-RNAseq) is public and its README lists four R Markdown files covering the downstream analysis (DE, WGCNA/PANGEA inputs, figures) together with the count matrices used as their input (smRNA_counts/, totRNA_Counts/HTSeq_Genes, totRNA_Counts/PropCount_Repeats). The upstream read-processing stage (trimming, QC, mapping, counting) has no corresponding script listed in the README prose, although the Methods text points to the same repository for the 'custom proportional counting script'; that discrepancy is recorded, not resolved, at stage 1. No version pin for any tool appears anywhere in the Methods prose or in the README, and the repository has no tags and no releases. Wet-lab procedures counted in W, not verdicted. Stage-1 reading only: no code files were read line by line.

steps.label: Total RNA-seq read trimming with trimgalore, minimum read length 20 bp ('Fastq files were trimmed using trimgalore with a minimum read length of 20bp')
Read quality assessment with FastQC ('FastQC was used to assess the quality of the remaining reads')

Total RNA repeat mapping to a heterochromatin-enriched genome with Bowtie2 (Langmead & Salzberg 2012); reference is the Chang & Larracuente 2019 heterochromatin-enriched assembly cited elsewhere in Methods
Total RNA gene mapping to the heterochromatin-enriched genome with STAR (Dobin et al. 2013)
Gene-level expression counting with HTSeq (Anders et al. 2015); output matrices appear in the repository as totRNA_Counts/HTSeq_Genes per the README

Repeat-level expression counting with a custom proportional counting script ('a custom proportional counting script (for repeats; https://github.com/LarracuenteLab/SD-RNAseq)'); output matrices appear as totRNA_Counts/PropCount_Repeats per the README, but the README file list does not name the script itself
Differential expression of total RNA genes and repeats with DESeq2 (Love et al. 2014); implemented in Rsp_SD_totRNA.rmd per README, run against the repository count matrices
Gene-set enrichment with PANGEA (Hu et al. 2023); significance threshold Benjamini-Hochberg FDR < 0.05; results CSVs deposited in the repository under PANGEA_Results/

WGCNA co-expression analysis (Langfelder & Horvath 2008) using the WGCNA R package: 50th percentile of variable genes, minimum R^2 = 0.8, Spearman correlation; difference between non-driving (R16/Gla) and driving (SD-Mad/Gla, SD-5/Gla) genotypes; significance by t-test with Tukey multiple-hypothesis correction
Small RNA read trimming for quality and length with cutadapt, minimum length 18 and maximum length 32

Depletion step: mapping trimmed small RNA reads to a library of rRNAs and tRNAs, retaining unmapped reads ('Remaining reads were then mapped to a library of rRNAs and tRNAs and unmapped reads were saved to a separate file')
Small RNA mapping of rRNA/tRNA-unmapped reads to the heterochromatin-enriched genome with Bowtie (Langmead et al. 2009)

Counting of miRNAs and complex satellite repeats with a custom python script assigning reads to features by the proportion of the read mapping to that feature (https://github.com/LarracuenteLab/SD-RNAseq); the README lists the resulting counts (smRNA_counts/, all_summedbyFam) plus TE_Families.tsv and miRNA.list, but not the script
Differential expression of small RNAs with DESeq2 (Love et al. 2014); implemented in Rsp_SD_smRNA.rmd per README, run against the repository small RNA count matrices

Figure-panel generation in R Markdown (Rsp_SD_Figures.rmd, with shared functions/packages in Rsp_SD_Code.Rmd which the README marks 'RUN FIRST'); supplementalTables named as the destination directory for generated tables

headline.static_readiness: 0/15 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: All 15 computational steps cap at NI at stage 1 because the version axis is 0 for every step: no version number is stated for any tool in the Methods prose (trimgalore, FastQC, cutadapt, Bowtie, Bowtie2, STAR, HTSeq, DESeq2, PANGEA, WGCNA, R itself), the README carries no version or environment information, and the repository has zero tags and zero releases. Under an inference-inclusive reading the ceiling would be 5/15 steps at RI (C7, C8, C9, C14, C15 - the downstream R analyses, whose input count matrices and R Markdown are both in the public repository); the 10 upstream steps (C1-C6, C10-C13) would remain NI regardless, because the raw sequencing data has no accession ('All genomic data are being deposited in NCBI's short read archive and an accession ID is forthcoming') and the read-processing scripts are not listed in the repository README prose.
headline.coverage: 15 computational steps assessed from Methods prose plus the repository README file list; 9 wet-lab steps counted (W) but out of computational-reproduction scope (fly stocks/crosses; CRISPR generation of SD-Mad Rev; CRISPR generation of the RspOE_DsRed 38C1 insertion line; testis RNA extraction and cDNA synthesis; RT-PCR; qRT-PCR with delta-delta-Ct quantification; RNA FISH; confocal imaging; k-value drive assays; library prep and Illumina HiSeq2500 sequencing - grouped to 9). Data availability and code availability statements are both present but the data statement carries no accession.

gaps.where: Software environment for all 15 computational steps
gaps.missing: No version pin exists for any tool anywhere in the paper or the repository landing page: trimgalore, FastQC, cutadapt, Bowtie, Bowtie2, STAR, HTSeq, DESeq2, PANGEA, the WGCNA R package and R/Bioconductor itself are all named without versions. No conda environment, renv lockfile, requirements file, sessionInfo record, or container is claimed. The repository has no tags and no releases, so even the code state cannot be addressed by version.
gaps.how_to_close: Record exact versions for every tool (or ship a conda-lock / renv.lock / container digest), and cut a tagged release or Zenodo deposit of the repository at the state used for the manuscript.

gaps.where: Raw sequencing data for all upstream steps (C1-C6, C10-C13)
gaps.missing: Data availability statement reads verbatim: 'All genomic data are being deposited in NCBI's short read archive and an accession ID is forthcoming.' No SRA/BioProject accession is present, so no raw small RNA or total RNA fastq can be obtained. The Dryad deposit for 'all code and data underlying analyses' is likewise stated as 'DOI forthcoming'.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the SRA/BioProject accession and the Dryad DOI, and cite them explicitly in the data availability statement.

gaps.where: Upstream read-processing steps C1-C6 and C10-C13
gaps.missing: The repository README lists only four R Markdown files (Rsp_SD_Code.Rmd, Rsp_SD_smRNA.rmd, Rsp_SD_totRNA.rmd, Rsp_SD_Figures.rmd) plus data/annotation files. No trimming, QC, mapping, or counting script or command line is listed, even though the Methods text cites this repository as the location of the 'custom proportional counting script' for repeats and the custom python small RNA counting script. The trimming-to-counting stage is therefore not re-runnable from the published artifacts as described in prose.
gaps.how_to_close: Add the read-processing scripts (trimgalore/cutadapt invocations, Bowtie/Bowtie2/STAR index build and alignment commands, HTSeq call, and both custom proportional counting scripts) to the repository and list them in the README, or ship the whole upstream stage as a workflow (Snakemake/Nextflow).

gaps.where: Reference genome and annotation for C3, C4, C5, C11, C12
gaps.missing: The 'heterochromatin enriched genome' is cited only by publication (Chang & Larracuente 2019) in a different Methods subsection, with no accession, release, or file checksum. The gene annotation used by HTSeq, the repeat/satellite annotation used by the proportional counting scripts, and the rRNA/tRNA library used for small RNA depletion are all undefined as retrievable artifacts (TE_Families.tsv and miRNA.list in the repository are family/ID mappings, not the reference sequences or GTF).
gaps.how_to_close: Pin the assembly and annotation by accession plus version or checksum, and deposit the rRNA/tRNA depletion library and the repeat annotation used for proportional counting.

gaps.where: Parameters for C2, C3, C4, C5, C10 (adapter), C11, C12
gaps.missing: Mapping parameters are entirely absent for Bowtie, Bowtie2 and STAR (multi-mapping policy is load-bearing for repeat quantification and is not stated). No adapter sequence is given for cutadapt, only length bounds (18-32). No HTSeq mode (union/intersection, stranded flag) is stated despite stranded library prep. DESeq2 design formulas and shrinkage/testing settings are not in prose.
gaps.how_to_close: State the full command lines, or ship them as scripts; specify multi-mapping handling for repeat quantification and the HTSeq mode/strandedness.

gaps.where: C6, C13 custom proportional counting scripts
gaps.missing: The core repeat-quantification method - assigning reads to features 'according to the proportion of the read mapping to that feature' - is described in one sentence with no algorithmic detail, no thresholds, and no script visible in the repository README listing. This is the step on which the paper's central repeat-expression claims rest.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the scripts with documentation of the proportional-assignment rule, thresholds, and tie handling, and list them in the README.

gaps.missing: https://github.com/LarracuenteLab/SD-RNAseq is public (created 2025-12-01, last push 2025-12-02, default branch main) but has no license file, no tags, no releases, and no archival mirror. There is no immutable reference to the state of the code at submission time.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a license, tag the manuscript state, and archive to Zenodo/Software Heritage so a permanent identifier exists.

gaps.where: Wet-lab: fly stocks and crosses; CRISPR generation of SD-Mad Rev; CRISPR generation of RspOE_DsRed at the 38C1 piRNA cluster and Cre-mediated marker removal; testis RNA extraction; cDNA synthesis; RT-PCR; qRT-PCR and delta-delta-Ct analysis; RNA FISH; confocal imaging (Leica SP5); k-value drive assays; mirVana small/long RNA fractionation, TruSeq library prep and Illumina HiSeq2500 sequencing
gaps.missing: Wet-lab generation and measurement steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W, not verdicted.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; scope is the RNA-seq analysis pipeline.
